moment of construction (chicken-and-egg with its own not-yet-persisted

head_commit.message:
PR #6 second-pass hardening: atomic evidence resolution, real content hashing, gate/variant readiness linkage

Fixes seven further defects a follow-up audit found in the first PR #6 repair:

1. Source-evidence conflict recovery used a catch-then-query pattern that is
   unsafe on Postgres (a failed statement aborts the rest of the
   transaction, so the recovery query never ran). Replaced with
   store.mjs#findOrCreate, a single atomic INSERT...ON CONFLICT...RETURNING.
2. Owner gates and message variants could link to a policy-rejected
   opportunity because only existence was checked, not stage. Now requires
   stage:ready_for_message; preview mode tracks accepted and rejected
   opportunity ids in separate sets.
3. tenOfTenReadiness restores the true original 14 gates (the first repair
   had replaced three with unrelated technical ones) and adds the five
   gates this audit named as missing (revenue attribution, accepted paid
   delivery, suppression testing, kill-switch testing, incident recovery).
   Every gate now requires full evidence provenance (evidenceRef, source,
   measurementWindow, timestamp), not just a bare value.
4. content_hash is computed from real evidence content (url/excerpt/
   capturedAt/official/confidence/type), not signalKey or the record id;
   signalKey is now its own column (migration 007). A genuinely fresher
   re-crawl always gets its own evidence row -- history is preserved.
5. partner_route/offer/rejection now go through the same freshness/
   official-source/lane/suppression/contact-provenance checks opportunities
   get. rejection records require an explicit, canonical-registry-validated
   reason_codes field -- risks is never used as a reason code.
6. Owner gates now require currency === USD outright (no FX-conversion
   source exists in this version) -- raw cents from another currency can no
   longer satisfy the USD threshold.
7. Preview mode is now truly zero-write, including its own audit trail --
   the prior single disclosed batch-level audit row is removed.

213/213 deterministic tests pass, including new real-Postgres concurrency
tests proving two distinct opportunities can safely share one evidence row
under genuine concurrent load.

head_commit.message:
PR #7 repair: real runtime wiring, durable stage ordering, frozen cohort, pre-dispatch recheck

Repairs every finding in UBERBOND_CLAUDE_PR7_REPAIR_PACK_V1 (independent verdict:
REPAIR_REQUIRED). Full finding-by-finding account: docs/PR7_REPAIR_REPORT.md.

- C-P0-001: register Canon job handlers in the real worker.mjs (via job-handlers.mjs)
  and gate automatic scheduling behind a separate, explicit, default-false
  ACQUISITION_WORKERS_ACTIVE check in scheduler.mjs. No live provider required at
  startup; outbound stays disabled by default.
- C-P0-002: scheduleCanonCycle now enqueues only the first stage job; every stage
  handler enqueues the next one itself, with a stable singletonKey, only after its
  own work succeeds -- at any instant at most one Canon stage job for a given day
  can exist, so downstream stages cannot run before their predecessor even at queue
  concurrency > 1. A crash mid-stage resumes via DurableQueue's existing lease
  machinery and the chain continues exactly once.
- C-P0-003: the original campaign-activation.mjs hashed the FULL approved recipient
  set and required an exact match per single-recipient check -- structurally unable
  to ever pass for more than one member. Migration 009 adds campaign_cohort_members:
  exactly N individually-claimable rows per approval, atomically claimed via a new
  store.mjs#claimCohortMember conditional UPDATE (both backends; proven under real
  concurrent load against real Postgres).
- C-P0-004: autonomous-cycle.mjs#runDispatch now re-runs the full canonical
  eligibility check transactionally, immediately before any provider invocation --
  a suppression, reply, or approval expiry arriving after reservation but before
  dispatch now blocks it; the provider is never called for a cancelled reservation.
- C-P0-005/006: every reservation is now patched with its canonical message
  (messageVariantId/contentHash/subject/body) and full attribution linkage
  (opportunityId/sourceEvidenceId/experimentId/lane/cohortApprovalId/prospectId)
  before send-planning considers it done. New src/attribution-chain.mjs proves the
  full chain is reconstructable from a single reservation.
- C-P1-001/002: the seven-day acceptance test is rewritten to drive the real
  DurableQueue and registered handlers at concurrency 3, with the clock injected
  through every stage's payload, including one genuine stale-job recovery mid-run.

Also fixes tests/postgres-schema.test.mjs, whose migratedDb() helper never actually
included migrations 008/009 -- they had never been validated against real Postgres
until this repair.

npm run check: 317/317 pass, 0 regressions. lite/ remains zero-diff.

head_commit.message:
Fix payment-truth overcounting bug; add offer compiler and command center

Trajectory audit found the current wedge (evidence-backed website
audits) is sound; the gap is commercial-loop integrity, not the
business model. This wave hardens the payment layer and adds
visibility into what's actually blocking the first dollar.

Confirmed real bug: subscription_updated (a metadata-only Lemon
Squeezy webhook fired on card/plan/renewal-date changes, never a new
charge) previously triggered unlockLead() and created a fresh
revenueEvents "sale" row on every occurrence -- overcounting gross
revenue by the number of lifecycle webhooks received, not the number
of real charges. subscription_payment_success/_failed (the actual
renewal-charge and dunning-failure events) were never handled at all,
making real recurring revenue after the first payment invisible.

src/payments.mjs gains classifyPaymentEvent(): a pure, deterministic
classifier mapping the real Lemon Squeezy event taxonomy to
CLEARED_ONE_TIME_PAYMENT / CLEARED_SUBSCRIPTION_PAYMENT /
SUBSCRIPTION_LIFECYCLE_UPDATE / REFUND_OR_DISPUTE / PENDING_OR_UNCLEAR
/ DUPLICATE / INVALID_OR_UNSUPPORTED / REVIEW_REQUIRED. revenue.mjs's
handleLemonWebhook now runs every event through it before acting;
unlockLead is only ever called for genuinely cleared payments.
Refunds are recorded as negative revenueEvents so grossRevenue nets
them out automatically. Every decision is audited via
store.log('payment_classification', ...).

src/offer-compiler.mjs (new): pure function packaging existing
prospect/audit/score data into a structured offer for 5 products.
Every price comes from cfg.revenue; an unconfigured price (agency
white-label) is reported as NOT_CONFIGURED, never invented.

src/founder-command-center.mjs (new): read-only report composing the
operator summary, offer compiler, and revenue summary into checkout
readiness, offer readiness, delivery readiness, payment truth, and a
max-3-action owner queue. Verified against a real store: immediately
surfaces "checkout not configured" as the top blocking action when
checkout URLs are empty, reproducing the flagged gap in the running
system.

Diagnosed the failing Vercel deployment locally: the repo root has no
vercel.json and is a persistent Docker server (correctly configured
for Render/Railway instead); a Vercel project appears pointed at the
root rather than lite/, which does have its own working vercel.json
and passing deployment.

53 new hostile tests across three files. 251/251 tests pass in npm
run check.

head_commit.message:
Add the Revenue Safety, Recovery, and Audit Foundation

Four coherent subsystems, all reusing canonical models -- no parallel
queue, suppression, evidence, or revenue model was created:

1. Reservation recovery (src/reservation-recovery.mjs): a time-boxed,
   bounded, deterministic sweep for outboundReservations stuck at
   'reserved' or 'dispatching' past a timeout. Reuses the exact
   existing state machine: a stale 'reserved' row (provider never
   reached) is safely cancelled; a stale 'dispatching' row (provider
   outcome genuinely unknown) is reclassified to the existing
   'uncertain' state, which the guard already treats as a permanent
   replay-block -- so a recovered row can never be silently resent.
   No new status, no migration (the status column has no CHECK
   constraint). Concurrent/duplicate sweeps are deduplicated via the
   store's existing duplicate-id ConflictError mechanism rather than a
   bespoke lock, since PostgreSQL doesn't support nesting a second
   transaction inside the caller's.

2. Volume/quota unification: extracted countActiveOutboundReservations()
   into send-safety.mjs as the one canonical daily/hourly cap-counting
   helper. Both evaluateDeliverabilityGuard and
   JsonStore._reserveOutboundSendDirect now call it instead of
   maintaining two independent implementations that could silently
   drift. No limit or threshold changed -- every pre-existing
   send-safety/pipeline test still passes unmodified.

3. Transactional report-email audit: RevenueEngine.sendReportEmail now
   writes a report_email_audit receipt for every decision (kill-switch
   block, missing destination, provider-capability-absent, uncertain
   outcome, sent), and a provider exception sets
   lead.reportEmailAttemptStatus='uncertain' which onProspectComplete's
   auto-send gate now checks to prevent ever automatically retrying an
   unresolved external outcome. Deliberately kept separate from the
   cold-outreach guard, since the destination is self-submitted at
   public intake, not discovered or inferred.

4. Operator visibility (src/outbound-operator-summary.mjs): a read-only
   structured summary of reservation states, a stale-recovery dry-run
   preview, provider health, review requirements, and a deterministic
   next-safe-action string, reusing existing collections only.

59 new hostile tests across four files. Pre-existing suites re-run
standalone as regression checks after each refactor. 198/198 tests
pass in npm run check.

head_commit.message:
Wire the Deliverability Guard into Pipeline.maybeSend

Pipeline.maybeSend is the sole choke point every cold-outreach send
path (processProspect, processOutboundQueue, processFollowups) funnels
through. It now calls evaluateDeliverabilityGuard() twice: once as an
admission gate before any reservation is attempted, and once as a
final recheck immediately before the provider boundary, right after
the reservation transitions to 'dispatching'. Both decisions are
persisted as receipts via the existing store.log() audit writer
(type: deliverability_guard_decision) -- no new receipt system.

A second send path, RevenueEngine.sendReportEmail, was found and left
out of scope: it delivers a transactional email to a self-submitted,
consented address, not cold outreach, and already has its own
independent kill switch and idempotency. Documented in the handoff
rather than force-fit into the outreach-shaped guard.

deliverability-guard.mjs gained excludeReservationId (so the final
recheck doesn't flag the reservation the call itself just made as a
replay or ceiling breach) and an actionIdentity content hash
(recipient/message/evidence/authority/policy) distinct from the
stable idempotencyKey, plus workspaceId mapped to campaign.id.

Fixed a regression caught by the pre-existing send-safety test suite:
the admission guard's replay detection initially hard-denied any
repeat call against an already-sent or uncertain reservation, breaking
the pre-existing idempotent-confirmation contract those tests already
relied on. A denial that reduces to a pure idempotency-key replay is
now translated back to that contract; any other reason present still
hard-denies.

16 new pipeline-integration tests in
tests/pipeline-deliverability-guard.test.mjs, wired into
test:deterministic. 139/139 tests pass overall.

head_commit.message:
Add a deterministic Deliverability Guard for outbound preparation

Adds evaluateDeliverabilityGuard() (src/deliverability-guard.mjs): a
pure, read-only decision function that composes UberBond's existing
canonical safety primitives (suppression list, outbound-reservation
idempotency, sender-health pausing, contact/evidence eligibility,
country/business-hour gates) into a single explainable
ALLOW_LOCAL_PREPARATION / REVIEW_REQUIRED / DENY decision with a full
audit receipt (reason codes, evidence refs, policy version, authority,
suppression/dedup results, confidence, cost estimate, owner burden,
idempotency key, timestamp, reversible next step). It never calls a
provider and never mutates state; no new suppression/queue/evidence
model was created.

Extracted suppressionLookup() into send-safety.mjs as the one
canonical suppression check, and updated Pipeline.isSuppressed to use
it instead of duplicating the lookup.

Fixed a real determinism bug found while writing hostile tests: the
guard's staleness/expiry checks originally compared against real
wall-clock Date.now() instead of the decision's own date parameter,
so the same input snapshot could produce different decisions depending
on when the guard happened to run. All three call sites now use the
passed-in reference date.

Wired the new module and its 25-test hostile suite into check:syntax
and test:deterministic so neither is ever silently unverified.
